about.title: Isleton Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Isleton sits along the Sacramento River at the edge of the Delta, and in a town of about 804 people, a death rarely stays private. Public records for 2025 list no traffic deaths within city limits, which is welcome news, yet wrongful death claims arise from more than crashes on SR-160. A fall at a rental property, a medical error, a workplace incident, or a defective product can all leave a family with the same questions. California law gives a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring a claim; certain dependents and heirs may qualify after them. Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. Most families have two years from the date of death, and less time when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent attorney who works on contingency, so asking questions costs nothing.

whyChoose.title: Why Isleton Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: Standing in California is limited, with a spouse or domestic partner and children first in line and certain dependents or heirs after. An independent attorney can tell you plainly whether you qualify before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: The general limit is two years from the date of death, but claims involving a city, county, or state agency such as Caltrans carry a much shorter window. Connecting soon protects that time.

items.title: Free connection, contingency representation
items.desc: LawProactive charges nothing to match you with an attorney, and the attorneys in our network take wrongful death cases on contingency. If there is no recovery, there is no attorney fee.

items.question: Isleton recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Does that mean wrongful death cases don't happen here?
items.answer: Not at all. A single loss in a community this small is one too many, and wrongful death claims are not limited to road crashes. Deaths tied to medical care, workplaces, unsafe property, boating on the river, or defective products all fall under the same California law.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as the criminal case against the person responsible?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action brought by the family, and it can move forward whether or not prosecutors file charges. The civil case focuses on the family's losses, including funeral costs, lost support, and the loss of companionship and guidance.

items.question: My relative died in a crash on SR-160. Does it matter that it is a state highway?
items.answer: It can. If any part of the claim involves a government entity, such as a road agency, California requires a formal claim within a much shorter period than the usual two years. An attorney can sort out who may be responsible and which deadlines apply, which is why reaching out early helps.
